source_runtime_review.method_inheritance_and_dispatch: PASS: derived Method preserves base fields and adds pf; new exact-match dispatch takes derived Method; old identity path explicitly casts base and qualifies old namespace.
source_runtime_review.row_scope_prologue: PASS: actual PF8 production prologue visitor uses first && ws < row_scope_end; first is ws == scope_start. No prologue repeats at later S64 windows.
source_runtime_review.profile_identity: PASS source review: two BF16 layers compare output bits and 37 logical/work fields against frozen PF1, with nonaliased output/input. Runtime smoke is audited separately.
source_runtime_review.target_gate: 36 production-visitor cases cover scopes FULL/64/256 and degrees 0,1,7,8,9,63,64,65,127,128,129,257 with deliberate duplicate/unsorted source IDs. Independent static model additionally covers exhausted rows and lengths 0..320 at nonzero and near-uint32-limit scope starts.
source_runtime_review.gate_limits: This review does not constitute actual M64/M256 kernel numerical acceptance; performance matrix uses FULL only.

normalization: Strip instruction addresses, byte columns and comments.
Replace intra-function branch destinations by offsets from function start; retain external destination symbols.
Normalize RIP-relative displacement only; retain registers, non-relocation immediates, stack offsets and instruction order.
limits: Identity covers two complete nonprofile reducer functions; it is not whole-binary byte identity.
RIP-referenced constant data bytes are not independently compared here; frozen source/header hash checks are separate.
Static opcode sites are not executed counts: PF8 has distinct prologue and steady sites; dynamic request parity requires instrumented counters.
No direct vector memory references through rsp/rbp were found in six reducers. This syntactic screen is not a general proof about every possible aliased stack access.
Static vpmovdw site counts differ across PF policies because compiler control-flow layouts differ; arithmetic work and output gates remain necessary.
No AVX-AMX overlap, memory-level parallelism, cache-level attribution or DRAM-byte claim follows.
